title: Cap. V Obj. 3: as one exists receiving eternal life, so considered — only the faithful predestinated
latin: Obj. 3. Qualis existens accipit vitam aeternam, talis a Deo consideratus praedestinatus est ut acciperet: Sed solus fidelis accipit, et nemo alius: Ergo solus fidelis, idque ut consideratur fidelis, praedestinatus est ad accipiendam vitam aeternam.
pass_a: Objection 3. Of what sort existing one receives eternal life, of such sort considered by God he has been predestinated that he might receive it: But only the faithful receives, and no other: Therefore only the faithful, and that as he is considered faithful, has been predestinated to receive eternal life.
pass_b: Obj. 3. As one exists when receiving eternal life, so considered by God he was predestinated to receive it. But only the faithful receives, and no one else. Therefore only the faithful — and as considered faithful — was predestinated to receive eternal life.

title: Cap. V Obj. 3 Sol: Major ambiguous — reject prior existence-as-faithful; grant foresight of what God will make
latin: Sol. Major multum in se habet ambiguitatis. Nam si eo sensu capiatur, quasi omnis ad vitam praedestinatus, antecedenter ad hoc decretum praedestinationis, talis existeret in intuitu Divino, qualis futurus est in ipsa acceptione vitae aeternae, prorsus rejicienda est. Si vero haec sit illius propositionis mens, Quando Deus electos ad vitam destinat, simul ab aeterno prospicit, et intuetur quales sit eos effecturus, antequam ad vitam perducat, eosdemque, ut tales, in vitae aeternae possessionem introducendos contempletur, id quidem verissimum est, nec negari potest, nisi quis negare velit Deum praescire quae ipse est facturus.
pass_a: Solution. The Major has much ambiguity in itself. For if it be taken in that sense, as if every one predestinated to life, antecedently to this decree of predestination, existed of such sort in the Divine intuition as he will be in the very reception of eternal life, it is altogether to be rejected. But if this be the mind of that proposition, When God destinates the elect to life, at the same time from eternity he looks forward, and looks upon of what sort he will make them, before he leads them through to life, and contemplates the same, as such, to be introduced into possession of eternal life, that indeed is most true, and cannot be denied, unless someone wish to deny that God foreknows what he himself is about to do.
pass_b: Sol. The Major is highly ambiguous. If it means every one predestinated to life already existed in God's intuition, before the predestination decree, as he will be in receiving eternal life — reject it outright. But if it means: when God destinates the elect to life, he at once from eternity looks ahead and sees of what sort he will make them before leading them to life, and contemplates them as such to be brought into possession of eternal life — that is most true, and cannot be denied unless one denies that God foreknows what he himself will do.

lemmas.gloss: God foreknows what he will do

title: Cap. V Obj. 3 Sol: foresight of elects' faith inferred from election — Acts 13:48; Prosper on dignity
latin: At hoc concesso non elicitur electio ex antecedanea fidei praevisione: sed certa in Deo fidei electorum praevisio infertur ex antecedanea electione, juxta illud celebre dictum, Actor. xiii. 48. Crediderunt quotquot ordinati fuerunt ad vitam aeternam. Unde etiam recte dicatur, Deum praevidere illos omnes crediturus, antequam accipiant vitam aeternam, quos decreto praedestinationis ad hanc vitam aeternam accipiendam ordinavit. Quod itaque Prosper de charitate dixit, id de fide etiam constanter affirmamus, Hoc tanto et tam ineffabili bono nemo inventus est dignus: Sed quicunque electus est a Deo, factus est dignus, de lib. arbit. pag. 125. Non dixit doctissimus Pater, et Pelagianorum ac Semipelagianorum Mastigium, Quicunque consideratus et praevisus ab ipso Deo ut dono charitatis aut fidei praeditus, ille postmodum ab eo electus est, sed, Quicunque a Deo electus est, ille postmodum fidei et charitatis factus est particeps.
pass_a: But this being granted, election is not elicited from antecedent foresight of faith: but a certain foresight in God of the faith of the elect is inferred from antecedent election, according to that celebrated saying, Acts 13:48. As many as were ordained to eternal life believed. Whence also it may rightly be said that God foresees all those as about to believe, before they receive eternal life, whom by the decree of predestination he has ordained to receive this eternal life. What therefore Prosper said of charity, that we also constantly affirm of faith: Of this so great and so ineffable good no one has been found worthy: But whoever has been elected by God has been made worthy, On Free Will, p. 125. The most learned Father, and scourge of the Pelagians and Semipelagians, did not say, Whoever considered and foreseen by God himself as endowed with the gift of charity or faith, he afterward was elected by him, but, Whoever has been elected by God, he afterward has been made partaker of faith and charity.
pass_b: Granted that, election is not drawn from antecedent foresight of faith — rather a sure foresight in God of the elects' faith is inferred from antecedent election, per Acts 13:48: as many as were ordained to eternal life believed. So God rightly foresees as about to believe, before they receive eternal life, all whom by the predestination decree he ordained to receive it. What Prosper said of charity we also affirm of faith (On Free Will, p. 125): of this so great, ineffable good no one was found worthy; but whoever was elected by God was made worthy. That learned Father, scourge of Pelagians and Semipelagians, did not say: whoever considered and foreseen as endowed with charity or faith was afterward elected — but: whoever was elected by God afterward became partaker of faith and charity.

title: Cap. V Obj. 3 Sol: preconsidered as to-be-faithful for reception, not as already faithful for destinating
latin: Quicunque igitur vitam aeternam accepturus est, a Deo fuit praeconsideratus ut fidelis futurus, idque antecedenter ad acceptionem vitae aeternae: sed non fuit praevisus ut fidelis existens, idque antecedenter ad destinationem vitae aeternae. Hoc simili rem explicemus: Si quis in re bene lauta, conspecto misero et inope infante, statim apud animum suum decernat illum adoptare et optima haereditate donare, ita tamen ut non adeat hanc haereditatem priusquam ad annos pubertatis pervenerit, ac bonis literis et moribus excultus fuerit; vere dicamus hanc haereditatem tali personae consideratae ut indoctae, ut incultae, ut infanti, fuisse destinatam; at eadem haereditas tali personae consideratae ut excultae, ut doctae, ut puberi, fuit donata, idque ex destinato proposito adoptantis.
pass_a: Whoever therefore is about to receive eternal life was preconsidered by God as about to be faithful, and that antecedently to the reception of eternal life: but he was not foreseen as existing faithful, and that antecedently to the destination of eternal life. Let us explain the matter by this likeness: If someone of good estate, having seen a wretched and needy infant, at once decrees in his mind to adopt him and gift him with an excellent inheritance, yet so that he not enter upon this inheritance before he has reached the years of puberty, and has been cultivated with good letters and manners; we may truly say that this inheritance was destinated to such a person considered as unlearned, as uncultivated, as an infant; but the same inheritance was gifted to such a person considered as cultivated, as learned, as of age, and that from the destinating purpose of the adopter.
pass_b: So whoever will receive eternal life was preconsidered by God as about to be faithful — antecedent to receiving eternal life — but not foreseen as already existing faithful — antecedent to destinating eternal life. Likeness: a man of good estate sees a wretched needy infant and at once decrees to adopt him and gift an excellent inheritance, yet not to enter it before puberty and cultivation in letters and manners. Truly that inheritance was destinated to him considered unlearned, uncultivated, an infant; yet the same inheritance was gifted to him considered cultivated, learned, of age — from the adopter's destinating purpose.

title: Cap. V Obj. 3 Sol close: same pattern in eternal inheritance; Hague Collation already refuted
latin: Si in aeternae haereditatis destinatione atque donatione simile quid cogitemus, facile praedicti argumenti infirmitatem perspiciemus. Plura non addo, quia idem pene argumentum, quamvis paululum immutatum, adductum fuit in Collatione Hagiensi, et a nobis antea refutatum.
pass_a: If in the destination and donation of the eternal inheritance we think something similar, we shall easily perceive the weakness of the aforesaid argument. I add no more, because nearly the same argument, though a little changed, was brought forward in the Hague Conference, and was formerly refuted by us.
pass_b: Think the same pattern in destinating and gifting the eternal inheritance, and the weakness of their argument is plain. I add no more: nearly the same argument, slightly altered, was brought at the Hague Conference and already refuted by us.
